To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) very deep convolutional networks can be efficiently trained, (2) the dropout technique reduces overfitting in deep models, and (3) the combination of these two ideas results in state of the art, record breaking results on the large scale ImageNet visual recognition challenge 2010 and 2012 competitions.

(i) very deep convolutional networks can learn to classify ImageNet images into the 10000 classes, with better than human-level performance, and (ii) this is possible by using a simple and generic learning method, namely backpropagation through time with stochastic gradient descent.

(a) deep convolutional networks with the proposed ReLU nonlinearity achieved state-of-the-art results on classification of hand-drawn digits, and (b) the same convolutional network architecture, trained end-to-end with backpropagation, achieved state-of-the art results on large-scale ImageNet classification.

the problem of large scale visual recognition and we believe that we have shown that it is possible to achieve state of the art results using a large convolutional neural network that has been trained on a very large collection of high resolution images.
